newsitem.title: USA: Morrell Sioux City hog plant said cutting shift.
newsitem.headline: Morrell Sioux City hog plant said cutting shift.

text.p: John Morrell and Co's hog slaughter plant in Sioux City, Iowa, will cut production by one shift a day for an indefinite period starting on Monday, company sources said.
"It will be taken a week at a time, or as soon as margins improve," said one Morrell source, who declined to be named.
Morrell is owned by Smithfield Foods Inc. Morrell and Smithfield officials were not immediately available to comment.
The Sioux City plant generally runs two shifts and has a daily capacity of 15,000 to 16,000 head, the sources said.

Pork industry sources on Friday reported rumors of the Morrell cutbacks due to poor margins, with trade talk that Smithfield and Morrell facilities may cut back daily slaughter by a total of as much as 18,000 head.
Morrell operates a second hog slaughter plant at Sioux Falls, S.D., with estimated capacity of 15,000 head a day.

Smithfield operates a hog plant in Tar Heel, N.C., with a daily capacity of about 24,000 head and a plant in Smithfield, Va., with capacity of about 10,000. Another Smithfield subsidiary, Gwaltney of Smithfield Ltd, has a hog plant in Gwaltney, Va., with estimated capacity of 9,000 head.
